facts.statement: Nemicolopterus lived in the Jehol Biota 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: It lived in the Jehol Biota 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: The generic name Nemicolopterus combines Greek words meaning forest, dweller, and wing.
facts.quote: The generic name "Nemicolopterus" comes from the following Ancient Greek words: "Nemos" meaning "forest", "ikolos" meaning "dweller", and "pteron" meaning "wing".

facts.statement: The specific name crypticus comes from the Greek word for hidden.
facts.quote: The specific name crypticus is from "kryptos", meaning "hidden".

facts.statement: The type specimen of Nemicolopterus crypticus is cataloged as IVPP V-14377 and is housed in Beijing, China.
facts.quote: The type fossil specimen of N. crypticus, catalog number IVPP V-14377, is housed in the collection of the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing, China.

facts.statement: The fossil was found in the Aptian-age Jiufotang Formation, dating to 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil was collected from the Jiufotang Formation, which is of Aptian age (120 mya).

facts.statement: The fossil was discovered in western Liaoning Province in northeastern China.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the Luzhhouou locality of Yaolugou Town, Jianchang County, Huludao City, western Liaoning Province in northeastern China.

facts.statement: Nemicolopterus had a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters, making it smaller than almost all known pterosaur specimens.
facts.quote: It has a wingspan of slightly under 25 centimeters (10 in), making it smaller than all but a few specimens of hatchling pterosaurs.

facts.statement: Researchers debate whether Nemicolopterus was a distinct species or a hatchling of Sinopterus, with some arguing that early bone fusion indicates a juvenile status.
facts.quote: However, Darren Naish argued on his popular weblog that, due to the hypothesis that pterosaurs were highly precocial, bone fusion and ossification could have occurred very early in life, and that Nemicolopterus might in fact be a hatchling individual of the genus Sinopterus.

facts.statement: The original describers concluded the specimen was a sub-adult based on bone fusion in the toes, gastralia, and sternum.
facts.quote: Wang et al. (2008), who originally described the specimen, concluded that it was immature, citing the amount of bone fusion and the ossification of the toes, gastralia, and sternum as indicating that it was a sub-adult rather than a hatchling.

facts.statement: A 2021 study formally identified Nemicolopterus as a young juvenile or hatchling of the genus Sinopterus.
facts.quote: This identification was formally presented in 2021 study, which found that Nemicolopterus fit into a growth series as a young juvenile or hatchling Sinopterus.

facts.statement: A 2014 analysis placed Nemicolopterus in a sister group relationship with Sinopterus gui.
facts.quote: An analysis of pterosaur relationships by Andres and colleagues in 2014 found the specimen in a sister group relationship with "Sinopterus" gui.

facts.statement: A 2023 revision concluded that Nemicolopterus could not be assigned to Sinopterus or Huaxiadraco and is now considered an indeterminate sinopterine.
facts.quote: A 2023 revision of Sinopterus concluded that it was impossible to assign the Nemicolopterus specimen to either Sinopterus or the new genus Huaxiadraco, and it was therefore considered an indeterminate sinopterine.

facts.statement: Nemicolopterus is classified within the unranked family Tapejaromorpha.
The time range for Nemicolopterus is estimated between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Nemicolopterus was originally described as the smallest known adult pterosaur based on a very small specimen.
rejected.quote: Nemicolopterus is a dubious genus of tapejaromorph pterosaur, based on a very small specimen originally described as the smallest known adult pterosaur to date.
